title: LastFiveHundredMetresLocationConfig
description: A reusable, building-level navigation config. One config per physical building/gate — NOT per delivery or per resident. Unit-specific details are passed at call-time, not baked in here, so one config serves every delivery to that building.

formal_address.description: Full postal address, for the record / fallback

type.description: e.g. 'pharmacy' — helps the agent disambiguate if the driver mentions a different pharmacy nearby

disambiguation_note.description: Only needed if there's a same-named or similar landmark nearby that could confuse the driver, e.g. 'not the Apollo Pharmacy near the metro station'

distinguishing_features.description: e.g. ['Blue and white building', 'XYZ Apartments signboard above entrance']

approach_from.description: One entry per direction a driver might arrive from. The agent's first real question to the driver is effectively 'which of these matches where you are' — so direction_label needs to be something a driver can self-identify against, not an internal code.

direction_label.description: e.g. 'Coming from the main road / Botanical Garden side'

instructions.description: e.g. 'Pass Apollo Pharmacy, take the second left.'

landmark_sequence.description: Ordered landmarks passed on this approach, optional, helps the agent re-orient if the driver is partway through and confused

identifying_marks.description: e.g. 'XYZ Apartments sign above the entrance'

access_notes.description: e.g. 'Security allows delivery drivers in without calling up'

units.description: Per-flat wayfinding for once the driver is inside the building. Optional — buildings with only one delivery point (a shop, a standalone house) can omit this entirely. Populated per-unit at config-authoring time; unit_identifier is looked up at call-time from the delivery, not passed as an arbitrary override.

unit_identifier.description: e.g. 'Flat 302' — must match how the resident/customer identifies their own unit

in_building_directions.description: e.g. 'Take the lift to the 3rd floor, it's the 2nd door on the left. No nameplate — look for the door with a black gate.'

escalation.description: Escalation is driver-confirmed, inside the same call, and resolves entirely within that call — no automated action after the call ends. If the driver confirms they want a real call, the agent reveals the customer's phone number to the driver and instructs them to call directly, then ends the call. No webhook, no second CALL-E call, no SMS.

trigger_conditions.description: Conditions under which the call-task instruction should OFFER escalation to the driver (not auto-trigger it), e.g. ['driver still can't locate landmark after 3 exchanges', 'driver reports landmark no longer exists']

contact_name.description: e.g. 'Sadiq' or 'the shop owner' — used when the agent tells the driver who they're calling

recipient_phone.description: Number the agent reads aloud to the driver on confirmed escalation, e.g. 'You can reach Sadiq directly at +14155550199.' The driver calls it themselves after this call ends.

allow_code_switch.description: Hinglish is normal in this context — don't force single-language rigidity

last_verified_at.description: Configs go stale — landmark pharmacies close, buildings get repainted. This field exists so a real product would know when to prompt a re-check. Not enforced for the hackathon, just modeled.
